transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, August 31. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. IPL media rights: Does the BCCI have a Plan B?. With JioStar the only serious bidder in sight, Indian cricket risks leaving value on the table Michael Dell shares a 'special note' for COO as he completes 39 years. Dell COO Jeff Clarke marked thirty-nine years with the technology company. This milestone coincides with Dell's major 'One Dell Way' transformation initiative. The company is consolidating multiple applications and systems into a single enterprise platform. This comprehensive change aims to simplify processes and enhance data flow across departments. Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism. Uzbekistan and India have elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Both nations unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in a joint statement. This marks a significant diplomatic alignment on regional security dynamics and counter-terrorism efforts. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and disrupting financing networks. Bizarre! Cricket team loses match due to broken print - here's how. Ballyspallen were forced to concede their Northern Ireland cricket match against Eglinton after a broken printer prevented officials from producing a required Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) sheet following rain. Eglinton had scored 159, while Ballyspallen were 19-0 when play stopped. League rules require the home side to concede if the DLS sheet cannot be provided to teams and umpires. Toxic Day 5 Box Office: Yash's film crosses rupees 200 cr, mints rupees 23 cr on Sunday. Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups continues its successful theatrical run. The Yash starrer has now surpassed rupees 200 crore in India net earnings. Its worldwide gross collection has reached rupees 285.20 crore after five days. The Hindi version contributed the most to the Day 5 India net collection. Two Malayali women killed in California; friend detained. THRISSUR/THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Two Malayali women were killed in California, United States, allegedly by another Malayali woman who was their friend and lived in the same apartment complex, according to their relatives. After renaming 'Gulf of Mexico' to 'Gulf of America', Google Maps changes name of 'Lake Ontario'. Google Maps has introduced a noteworthy update, displaying Lake Ontario as Lake America for American users. This decision aligns with a new presidential executive order and modifications to the GNIS. Canadian officials maintain the traditional name, highlighting its rich heritage over centuries. Meanwhile, alternative mapping platforms such as MapQuest and Apple Maps have not yet responded to this change, which is tailored regionally depending on the user's location. For every rupees 100 laundered, only Re 1 recovered by authorities: CJI Surya Kant. NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said for every rupees 100 laundered, authorities and law enforcement agencies recovered only Re 1, mainly because of the ingenuity of economic offenders, and lack of global cooperation on extraditing fugitives. Nepal Floods: Hunt intensifies for 900 missing at hydel units, one tunnel head located. As rescue operations intensify in Nepal, over 900 individuals remain unaccounted for in the aftermath of devastating floods that have led to 810 confirmed deaths in both Nepal and Tibet. Teams are utilizing advanced tools at the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project to search for survivors. Notably, several Indian nationals are among the missing, which has led India to provide crucial technical and relief assistance for the ongoing rescue efforts. Family seeks Medal of Honor for 23-year-old Korean War hero, 74 years after death. Sergeant Willie Estrada's family is urging for the highest military accolade, the Medal of Honor, in remembrance of his courageous sacrifice during the Korean War. Strikingly, he lost his life defending his tank crew near Bongowol, North Korea, in 1952. Honored posthumously with the Distinguished Service Cross, his loved ones are diligently working with legislators to officially document his remarkable legacy and heroism. 15 missing, 62 evacuated after flash flood hits Grand Canyon; more storms feared. An estimated 15 people may be missing and at least 62 have been evacuated after a powerful flash flood tore through parts of Arizona's Grand Canyon National Park, destroying footbridges and severely damaging infrastructure, park officials said.
